memos.risk:
Risk call on CATE: I'd refuse this one. Size $0.

Reasons: the curve is effectively controlled. Bundle share and top-3 share are both 1.0, and the top-5 buyers took 99.9% of the first two minutes after graduation (983 SOL, with 10 buyers ex-agent). Sell-to-buy in that window was zero, so nothing has been distributed yet. That is the operator setup, but the operator's exit hasn't happened, so there's no evidence yet that the supply is clean.

The last 15 minutes look like distribution: 8.38 SOL sold against 9.12 bought, 29 sellers, and a flat price. A $20 ticket into a ~1,078 SOL pool would also eat a meaningful share of the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost, and the drawdown and return data give no edge.

Refuse conditions: any operator-backed coin where the top buyers haven't yet exited, or where net flow turns negative after a flat print like this. If the desk ever did buy an operator coin, I'd cap at $5 with a 20% stop and a 15-minute hold, but this one doesn't clear the bar.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying CATE now is weak, and I can't make a strong one from this brief.

The strongest point is the 30-minute return of +3.8% with only a 0.03% drawdown from the 30-minute high, so the price has held without a dump. The last 15 minutes also show 43 buyers against 29 sellers, with 9.12 SOL bought and 8.38 SOL sold, a small net inflow of 0.75 SOL. That is the only signal of ongoing participation.

The rest argues against buying. The first two minutes after graduation saw 983 SOL bought by a single bundle, with the top five buyers taking 99.9% of flow and a launch bot present. This is an operator-backed coin, and the desk's own base rate for that class is roughly break-even before our 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost. The recent sell-side flow is nearly as large as the buy-side, and the top-three holder concentration is 100%, so one actor's exit could drain the pool. The pool depth of 1,078 SOL is deep enough to avoid heavy slippage, but depth does not create demand.

My conclusion: no real case for buying here. Skip it.
memos.skeptic:
Most likely loss: insider distribution by the operator. The first two minutes after graduation show 983 SOL bought by 10 buyers, with the top 5 holding 99.9% of that buying and a launch bot present. Bundle share and top-3 curve share are both 1.0, so essentially the whole supply sits with a handful of wallets that can exit at will. Pool depth is only 1,077.83 SOL, so a single large sell moves price hard, and our $20 ticket would be exit-liquidity behind them.

The last 15 minutes look like the start of that unwind: 8.38 SOL sold against 9.12 bought, sell-to-buy in the first two minutes is 0.0 (no early sellers, which suggests the holders are just waiting), and 29 sellers already active. The 30-minute high is essentially where it sits (drawdown 0.0003), so there is no dip to buy.

With round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1%, even a modest operator dump wipes out any small pop. Skip.
